stem.text: A wire consists of a $3.0\,\text{m}$ length of metal X joined to a $1.0\,\text{m}$ length of metal Y.
The cross-sectional area of the wire is uniform.

stem.alt: Vertical wire hung from a ceiling, with metal X labelled on the upper part and metal Y on the lower part, lengths 3.0 m and 1.0 m marked, and a load at the bottom

stem.text: A load hung from the wire causes metal X to extend by $1.5\,\text{mm}$ and metal Y to extend by $1.0\,\text{mm}$.
The same load is then hung from a second wire of the same cross-sectional area, consisting of a $1.0\,\text{m}$ length of metal X and a $3.0\,\text{m}$ length of metal Y.
Both wires are extended within their limit of proportionality.
What is the total extension of this second wire?
